html:
The attempt in 58 BCE by the Helvetii, a Celtic people of the Swiss plateau, to leave their homeland and settle in western Gaul. It became the first campaign of the Gallic Wars.

Hemmed in by mountains, lakes and the Rhine, and pressed by Germanic peoples to the north, the Helvetii planned the move for years. They burned their own towns and villages so no one would turn back. Julius Caesar, newly governor, refused them a road through the Roman province near Geneva, so they took a harder route over the Jura.

Caesar followed. He caught one clan, the Tigurini, crossing the Saône and destroyed them; the same clan had beaten a Roman army during the Cimbrian War. Then he beat the main body at the Battle of Bibracte. He sent the survivors home to rebuild, so the land would not fall to Germans.

Caesar says lists in Greek letters were found in their camp, counting those who left and those who returned. His numbers, given in his Gallic War, cannot be checked. The episode gave him his first excuse to march deep into Gaul.
